purpose: Define how pipeline-specific evidence is converted into the normalized three-valued primitive predicates consumed by the WH core adjudication procedure.
hard_rule: A pipeline-specific predicate contract must expose evidence fields, operator/categorical rule, threshold or allowed set where applicable, direction/polarity, missingness behavior, provenance/version, and output semantics. Missing mandatory evidence maps to UNKNOWN unless a separate integrity rule makes the object inadmissible.

primitive_predicates.input: all declared required hard-contract subpredicates for module m
primitive_predicates.rule: FAIL if any admissible subpredicate FAIL; PASS if all required subpredicates PASS; UNKNOWN if none FAIL and at least one mandatory subpredicate UNKNOWN
TRUE iff P01=FAIL; FALSE iff P01=PASS; UNKNOWN iff P01=UNKNOWN

primitive_predicates.input: admissible directed manifest graph, source module, affected node/invariant
primitive_predicates.rule: TRUE iff a declared directed path exists; FALSE iff graph is admissible and no path exists; UNKNOWN if required graph relation is not admissible/evaluable

primitive_predicates.input: versioned acceptance/invariant contract + declared evidence fields
primitive_predicates.rule: Evaluate the contract operator exactly; FAIL denotes invariant violation, PASS denotes satisfaction, UNKNOWN denotes missing/unevaluable mandatory input
Apply declared operator/threshold/category; TRUE=accepted, FALSE=not accepted, UNKNOWN=mandatory input not evaluable

primitive_predicates.input: admissible influence/provenance relation, declared sign/direction rule, upstream abnormality, downstream/endpoint evidence
primitive_predicates.rule: TRUE only when the frozen influence rule establishes an opposing/attenuating relation sufficient to explain masking; FALSE when the relation is contradicted; UNKNOWN when a required relation/sign/direction is unavailable

primitive_predicates.input: admissible candidate sources, dependency/path relations, observed downstream violations, path/global invariants, influence/provenance constraints
primitive_predicates.rule: Enumerate bounded source sets satisfying Section 2.4.6 explanation constraints, then remove every strict superset whose proper subset also satisfies the constraints
primitive_predicates.output: family of minimal source sets; unresolved family retained

primitive_predicates.input: topology-defining relations in Z + frozen primitive registry
primitive_predicates.rule: TRUE iff every topology-defining relation maps to a frozen primitive without introducing an unregistered relation/operator; FALSE if at least one relation is unmapped; UNKNOWN if relation identity is not evaluable

primitive_predicates.input: topology-defining relations in Z, compatible known topologies, primitive-decomposition result
primitive_predicates.rule: PRESENT iff a non-empty admissible relation set remains after known-topology representation and complete known-primitive decomposition; ABSENT iff none remains; UNKNOWN if required relation identity is unevaluable

primitive_predicates.input: predeclared inspection catalog + current UNKNOWN/competing decision predicate(s) + governance state
primitive_predicates.rule: TRUE iff at least one predeclared inspection can change a current decision-relevant UNKNOWN/competition and opening is authorized by the inspection contract; rank by higher discrimination, lower cost, stable ID

primitive_predicates.input: supported exact target + versioned repair mapping + falsifiable verification plan
primitive_predicates.rule: recommendation-sufficient only when all three exist at compatible granularity

primitive_predicates.input: authorized execution record + all prespecified re-audit predicates + protected-state invariants
primitive_predicates.rule: RESOLVED iff all mandatory checks PASS and protected invariants intact; any FAIL -> REOPENED_NOT_RESOLVED; mandatory UNKNOWN/unavailable -> HOLD

boundary: WH core does not impose universal domain thresholds. Pipeline-specific thresholds and categorical acceptance rules remain external, versioned contracts; the core consumes their auditable TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN or PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN outputs.
